title: Compile strategy rotation and pin safety for hybrid expert-routing models
creator: Priya Shah
description:
Problem: Hybrid architectures (multiheaded MHA, grouped-query attention, and MoE models) are showing varied latency and memory behavior across hardware families. Our current onboarding publishes a single 'best' kernel profile and pins models to it, which leads to regression risk when traffic patterns shift (sequence length, batch mix, expert fanout). Goal: implement a compile/dispatch strategy rotation and safe pin lifecycle so we can publish multiple competing kernel bundles, automatically prefer low-latency/cost bundles in steady state, and fall back gracefully when regressions or capacity events occur.

Scope:
- Add model-level 'rotation' metadata so a model can be assigned an ordered set of compiled bundles (e.g., bundle-A: fp16-cu, bundle-B: int8-cu-quant, bundle-C: nvfuser).
- Implement runtime routing to prefer the top-ranked bundle but route a configurable fraction of traffic to healthy alternates for canarying, warm caches, and metric estimation.
- Introduce a pin-aging policy: pins have TTL and auto-demote if telemetry shows degradation (latency P95 increase > 15% or error rate increase > 0.3%).
- Safety nets: fast binary-compatible rollback, shadow routing for bundle validation, and a forced 'fallback chain' mapping to ensure functional correctness (e.g., kernel semantic variants map to a CPU-safe path).
- Telemetry and signals: add new metrics (bundle_request_count, bundle_latency_p50/p95, bundle_qps, bundle_fallback_rate) and implement a composite health score used for rotation decisions.
- Onboarding UX: extend existing model onboarding form with 'rotation_candidates' field, compatibility matrix hinting (recommended bundles by arch + seq_len range), and automated rollout templates.

Out-of-scope: automated compile tuning heuristics (we will consume outputs from the autotuner pipeline separately) and new kernel implementations. This ticket focuses on lifecycle, routing, telemetry, and safety policies that enable safe multi-bundle publishing.
acceptance_criteria: Runtime can associate a model with an ordered list of compiled bundles and persist that mapping to model metadata
Routing respects bundle weights: default 90% top-bundle, 10% distributed to alternates (configurable per-model)
Telemetry for each bundle emitted to metrics backend and visible in Console per-model dashboard
Pin-aging demotes a bundle automatically when composite health score falls below configured threshold and promotes a healthy alternate
Rollout Playbook documented with exact rollback steps and automated rollback runbook in Console
Integration tests cover: routing weights, fallback chain, bundle demotion on synthetic latency regressions, and ACLs for private customers
